newsitem.title: USA: OMB urging broad US aid plan for ailing DC -- source.
newsitem.headline: OMB urging broad US aid plan for ailing DC -- source.

text.p: The Office of Management and Budget is recommending that the U.S. government pay more of the District of Columbia's Medicaid bills, assume prison costs for city felons and pay millions of dollars in unfunded pension liability handed to the city in 1974 when it won Home Rule, knowledeable sources said.
In return, the city would forfeit an annual $660 million payment it gets from Congress to offset what it loses from tax-exempt federal properties, said one source, who asked not to be identified.

Currently, the District and federal government each pay 50 percent of Medicaid reimbursement costs for D.C. citizens. The source said OMB will recommend the federal share be hiked, but he did not know by how much.

On prisons, the source said the U.S. would assume the costs of imprisoning D.C. felons, but it is not clear whether or not the federal government would ship prisoners to other federal jails, or use existing city facililties.
The source also said OMB would call for a transition period to give D.C. and the federal government time to make the shift.

"You can't (immediately) transfer 7,000 felony inmates out of Lorton and send them around to federal prisons," the source said, referring to D.C. Department of Corrections at Lorton, Va. "They don't have 7,000 beds (out) there.
"By the same token, you can't expect the federal Bureau of Prisons to walk in next week with 3,500 new corrections take over the existing prisons."
Another source said OMB is recommending the federal government take over some of the costs of the city's estimated $5 billion unfunded pension liability.
Also under consideration is having the Internal Revenue Service take over collection and enforcement of local income taxes.

White House spokesman Michael McCurry described as "speculation" a Wall Street Journal report this morning that the Clinton Administration soon will unveil an aid package for D.C. that calls on the U.S. to assume city costs for Medicaid, pensions and prison program.
But he added: "We told you all along we are looking for some ways we can address needs of the District. There will be more to say on that when the budget is announced" in February.
"I can't detail any of the specifics. I can tell you the President has been working on this. So has Director Raines of the OMB," he said, referring to OMB chief Franklin Raines.
"The President is committed and will remain committed to addressing the needs of the District."
